page: Microsoft Azure B1s is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the BS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a single vCPU mapped to one physical core and one thread, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture operating at 2.6 GHz. The processor cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 50 MB of L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 1.0 GB of system memory and 4 GB of local storage, and it supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data places this server in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both register at 1335.88, reflecting the single-threaded nature of the hardware. Memory bandwidth is limited, with read-only small block cached operations reaching 90.14 GB/sec, while large block uncached read and write operations drop to 10.85 GB/sec and 8.84 GB/sec respectively. Passmark CPU scores are low, with a base score of 1446.1 and a physics test score of 196.54. Redis SET operations achieve 1.49 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 1.45 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the B1s is positioned as a low-resource, budget-friendly option. The burstable CPU allocation model allows the instance to handle occasional spikes in traffic or processing demands without requiring the continuous allocation of dedicated high-performance resources. However, the limited 1.0 GB of RAM and low overall benchmark scores present significant tradeoffs, making it unsuitable for memory-intensive applications or sustained heavy compute workloads. Appropriate workloads are restricted to lightweight tasks such as small-scale static web serving, minor development or testing environments, and simple background processes that tolerate variable CPU performance.
